components.note: 夭 (a person leaning back) — the pose of someone laughing.
⺮ (bamboo-like strokes) — suggesting a wide grin, giving 笑 its meaning 'to laugh, smile.'
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'
丁 (a stylized handle/hook shape in the ancient form) — part of the character's original picture, now mostly opaque in the modern form
口 (kǒu, mouth) gives a sound related to 可's pronunciation kě, and may connect to 可's sense of approval spoken aloud
忄 (heart) — 惜 describes an emotional response felt in the heart.
昔 (the past, former times) — feeling 忄 for the past 昔 gave 惜 its meaning 'to cherish, to regret.'
口 (a rock) — the boulder itself.
厂 (a cliff) — the rock lying at the base of a cliff, the source of 石's meaning 'stone, rock.'
大 (big) — in 头's simplified form, this element is linked to the idea of 'high' or topmost, since the head sits at the top of the body.

meanings: foot (unit of length equal to 0.3048 m)

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 英 originally meant 'flower, blossom,' later borrowed for 'outstanding, hero' and to write 'England, English.'
央 (yāng) gives a sound hint — 英 is pronounced yīng, sharing the initial consonant and a nasal final, though the vowel has shifted.
尺 is traditionally read as a picture of a bent leg taking a measured step, used before rulers existed to pace off a distance — the origin of its meaning 'a Chinese foot, a ruler.'
纟 (silk/thread) — 细 relates to something as fine and thin as silk thread
田 (tián) gives a loose sound connection to 细's reading xì
节 is the simplified form of 節, which depicted the segmented sections of a bamboo stalk ⺮ — giving 节 its meaning 'joint, section, festival.'
禾 (grain, a rice/wheat plant) — 科 relates to sorting and measuring crops.
斗 (a measuring ladle) — measuring grain into ordered categories gave 科 its meaning 'a branch of study' or 'a department.'
冖 (a covering/roof) — represents the building or schoolhouse where learning happens.
子 (child) — 学 depicts children gathered to study.
⺍ is a small graphic element at the top of the character; its original pictorial meaning, if any, has been lost over time.
月 (yuè) here actually derives from 肉 (meat) — 有 originally depicted a hand holding meat, meaning 'to possess'; it also lends a loose phonetic connection to yǒu.
辶 (to walk) — 道 relates to a path or road one walks along.
首 (shǒu) is the historical phonetic element; its modern reading no longer resembles dào, a reminder that sound components can drift after thousands of years of pronunciation change.
王 (a variant form of 玉, meaning jade) — 理 originally referred to the natural grain or pattern in jade, later extending to 'reason, logic, to manage.'
里 (lǐ) gives the sound — 理 is also pronounced lǐ, an exact match.
舟 (boat) — 船 is a vessel that travels on water, directly tied to its meaning 'ship, boat'
长 (simplified from 長) depicts an elderly figure with long flowing hair and a cane — length and seniority are linked in the original picture.
欠 (breath, an open mouth exhaling) — 歌 relates to the breath used in singing.
哥 (gē) gives the sound — an exact match with 歌's reading gē.
手 is a simple picture of an open hand with the fingers spread out.

meanings: high ranking officer in Chinese army

components.note: A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
木 (wood) — 校 originally related to a wooden framework, later coming to mean 'school,' a place of structured learning
交 (jiāo) gives a sound close to 校's reading xiào
辶 (walking/movement) — relates to 运's meaning 'to move, transport,' and by extension 'fortune,' the movement of one's life.
云 (yún) gives a sound hint — 运 is pronounced yùn, sharing the same base sound with a different tone.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
丶 (a dot) — represents the burning flame atop a lamp.
王 here depicts the base and stand of an oil lamp, not its usual meaning 'king' — the one who tends the flame became linked to 'master, lord, main.'
女 (woman) with 覀 depicting hands on the waist — an old image of insisting or demanding something, connected to 要's meaning 'to want, to need.'
凡 (common/ordinary) — suggests something shared or held in common.
口 (mouth) — sharing a common mouth/voice with others gave 同 its meaning of 'same, together.'
食 (food) — 餐 relates directly to eating and meals.
广 (a building/shelter) — 厅 names a large room inside a building, a hall.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound close to tīng.
羊 (sheep; here representing feathers or ornaments on a headdress) — an elaborate decoration worn on the head.
大 (a person, arms outstretched) — a person wearing a decorated headdress was seen as beautiful, giving 美 its meaning 'beautiful.'
女 depicts a kneeling figure with arms crossed, a traditional posture — a simple picture of a woman.
足 (foot) — 距 relates to the distance covered on foot.
巨 (jù) is an exact match for the sound of 距.
亠 — read as the head of an animal standing upright in this pictograph; the character was later reused for the unrelated meaning 'to leave, be apart from, distance.'
讠 (speech) — 讲 relates to speaking, explaining, telling
井 (jǐng) gives a sound close to 讲's reading jiǎng
讠 (speech) — 话 relates to speaking and words.
舌 (tongue) — the organ used for speaking, reinforcing 话's meaning of 'speech' or 'words.'

户 (door) — 所 evokes a location or place, such as where a door stands.
斤 (axe) — combined with 户 (door), the image of an axe at a door gave rise to the abstract sense of 'a place' or 'that which.'
刂 (knife) — 制 relates to cutting and shaping, and by extension, to making or controlling something.
巾 (jīn) gives a hint of the sound — 制 is pronounced zhì, a connection that has drifted over time.
亻 (person) plus 乍 (suddenly/for the first time) — together suggesting a person making or doing something for the first time.
行 (to go/walk) — 街 names a road where people walk and travel.
圭 (guī) gives a sound distantly related to jiē, having drifted apart over time.
A short stroke placed above a longer one — a simple graphic way to show 'up' or 'above,' contrasted with 下 (down), which flips the strokes.
才 (talent) — many talented people.
囗 (an enclosure) — gathered together in one place, giving 团 its meaning 'group, team; round, ball-shaped.'
阝 (a mound or place) — 队 pictures people gathering together.
人 (person) — people gathering in one place gave 队 its meaning 'a team' or 'a line/queue.'
日 (sun) — represents the sun.
十 depicts the first rays of sunlight appearing low on the horizon — together with 日 (sun) giving 早 its meaning 'early, morning.'
尤 (particularly/outstanding) — relates to 就's sense of approaching or arriving at a particular point
京 (jīng, capital) gives a sound close to 就's pronunciation jiù
自 (originally a picture of a nose) — 鼻 names the nose.
畀 (bì) gives a sound close to bí, differing only in tone.
A simple drawing of a swaddled baby — arms reaching out, legs bundled together in a wrap.
木 (tree) — 相 pictures looking closely at a tree.
目 (eye) — staring closely at a tree to examine it gave 相 the meaning 'to observe' or, later, 'each other, mutual.'
夂 (a foot, to go) — 处 relates to arriving somewhere.
卜 (a mark or flag) — planting a marker after arriving gave 处 its meaning of 'a place' or 'to settle, deal with.'
罒 (a net) — something trapped inside it.
去 (to leave, go) — unable to get away, together giving 罢 its meaning 'to stop, cease.'
Depicts a child wrapped in swaddling, related to 子 (child); the picture-meaning has nothing to do with its modern grammatical role marking a completed action or change of state.
广 (a building or shelter) — 度 pictures people gathering indoors.
廿 (twenty) — a group of people meeting to measure or deliberate gave 度 its meaning of a 'degree' or 'measure,' as in temperature or angles.
辶 (to walk/move) — shows 过's core meaning of 'passing through' or 'crossing'
咼 (guō) gives a sound close to 过's reading guò; the simplified form 过 now uses 寸 in place of 咼, but the phonetic connection traces back to the traditional character 過
氵 (water) — 注 relates to pouring or directing, like water poured into something
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to 注's reading zhù
心 (heart/mind) — 德 relates to inner moral character and virtue.
囗 (a boundary/enclosure) surrounding 玉 (jade, treasure) — a country pictured as protected, valuable territory.
A drawing of a person standing with arms and legs spread wide — used to represent the idea of something being 'big' or 'great.'
阝 (a variant of 邑, meaning place/settlement) — 部 relates to a division, section, or department.
咅 supplies the sound for 部 (bù); it belongs to the same phonetic family as related characters like 倍 (bèi) and 培 (péi).
八 (to divide/split apart) — represents something already split into parts.
刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
穴 (hole/cave) — 窗 originally described an opening for light and air.
囱 (cōng) gives a sound distantly related to chuāng, having drifted apart over time.
户 (a simplified form of 戶) depicts a single door panel swinging on its hinge.

meanings: variant of 奇蹟|奇迹[qi2 ji4]

components.note: 大 (a person, arms outstretched) — represents a rider.
可 here is said to depict a mount — a person riding in an unusual way gave 奇 its meaning 'strange, odd, remarkable.'
辶 (to walk) — 迹 names the trace left behind by walking.
亦 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to jī, having drifted apart over time.
穴 (a cave/hole) — 空 relates to an empty hollow space.
工 (gōng) gives a hint of the sound — 空 is pronounced kōng, a connection that has drifted over time.
气 (simplified from 氣) depicts rising wisps or vapor, like breath or steam drifting upward — a simple picture of air or gas.
扌 (hand) — represents the act of guarding or defending.
户 (door/household) — protecting one's home gave 护 its meaning 'to protect, guard.'

meanings: to share (esp. sth enjoyable, useful or beneficial)

刀 (knife) — a knife cutting already-divided pieces further, giving 分 its meaning 'to divide, to separate.'
亠 (a roof) — the top of a house.
口 (a mouth) — eating and enjoying inside it.
子 (a child) — together showing a family living and eating well under one roof, giving 享 its meaning 'to enjoy.'
衤 (clothing) — 被 originally meant a quilt or covering, like a blanket.
皮 (pí) gives a hint of the sound — 被 is pronounced bèi, a connection that has shifted over time.
扌 (hand) — 捕 describes catching something with the hands.
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound close to bǔ, sharing the same kind of initial consonant.
Heart — regret is an emotional response.
Gives the sound měi, related to huǐ but drifted apart over time.
卬 depicts a person looking upward — 仰 keeps that upward gaze.
亻 (person) — a person 亻 looking upward 卬 gave 仰 its meaning 'to look up to, to admire.'
亻 (person) — 保 relates to a person looking after or protecting someone, originally a caretaker holding a child.
呆 (dāi) gives a hint of the sound — 保 is pronounced bǎo, a connection that has shifted over time.
宀 (a roof, house) — 安 pictures shelter.
女 (woman) — a woman safely inside a house gave 安 its meaning 'peace' or 'safety.'
心 (heart/mind) — 态 relates to one's inner state, manner, or attitude
太 (tài) gives the sound — 态 is also pronounced tài, an exact match
女 (woman) — 媒 originally described a woman who arranged marriages, 'a matchmaker.'
某 (mǒu) is only distantly related in sound to méi — the connection has drifted apart over time.
走 (to walk, to run) — 赶 relates to pursuing or hurrying, both forms of movement.
干 (gān) gives a rhyme close to gǎn, with the tone shifted.
糸 (silk/thread) — 紧 relates to something pulled taut, as thread is pulled tight when spun, giving its meaning 'tight, tense'
